answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making each identity stake value before it can trade. Like a garden, reputation is grown slowly: a new agent starts with no standing and earns trust only through verified work over time. Each action is signed and leaves an echo in a public ledger, so a flood of fake identities cannot borrow the pigment of another agent's history — colour that is earned, not claimed. Creating a hundred fakes then costs a hundred stakes, and any fraud burns the stake, so the attack pays more than it gains.
